q-159878.name: Question 1
q-159878.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14192941/assets/f1d9c516171eade5488c3247bd20d0bfcafd515e4da7de8aee3fe35174a87e8b.png)

On which interval is the function $y=f(x)$, shown above, strictly increasing?
q-159878.worked_solution:
If we follow the graph from left to right, we can see that: 

- For $x\in (-\infty ,-2)$ the graph falls

- For $x\in (-2,0)$ the graph is flat

- For $x\in (0,2)$ the graph rises

- For $x\in (2,\infty )$ the graph falls

The function is strictly increasing on the intervals where it always rises: $(0,2)$ only.

Question 3
?

On which interval is the function y=f(x), shown above, decreasing?

a
(−∞,−3) and (3,∞)
b
 (−3,−2), (−1,0), (1,2), and (3,∞)
c
 (−∞,−3), (−2,−1), (0,1), and (2,3)
d
(−3,−1), (−1,1), and (1,3)
e
 (−∞,−3), (−2,−1), (1,2), and (3,∞)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

If we follow the graph from left to right, we can see that:

  • For x∈(−∞,−3) the graph falls

  • For x∈(−3,−2) the graph rises

  • For x∈(−2,−1) the graph falls

  • For x∈(−1,0) the graph rises

  • For x∈(0,1) the graph falls

  • For x∈(1,2) the graph rises

  • For x∈(2,3) the graph falls

  • For x∈(3,∞) the graph rises

The function is decreasing on the intervals where it never rises: (−∞,−3), (−2,−1), (0,1), and (2,3).
